R226.note: Adds the *jwt.SigningMethodHMAC assertion inside keyFunc, the idiomatic golang-jwt guard; nothing else changes but a comment and the fmt import.

R227.note: Correct pre-addition overflow guard (headerLen > max - payloadLen) using <limits>; the new nullptr return fires only on inputs that previously produced the undersized allocation and is stated in the write-up.

R228.note: Authorization is keyed to a self-asserted x-user-id metadata header that nothing verifies, so any caller can claim the owner's id; the ChainUnaryInterceptor is also inert because the case's hand-written MethodDesc handler ignores its interceptor argument, and the fix newly requires that header plus users.is_admin / projects.owner_id columns not present in the case.

R229.note: Pins algorithms: ['RS256'] on jwt.verify, matching the documented issuance; no other behaviour or error path changed.

R230.note: Named parameter :searchPattern with the wildcards concatenated into the bound value preserves the original LIKE semantics exactly.

R231.note: RESP array with byte-accurate bulk-string length prefixes makes CRLF in bio data rather than syntax; the array count, encoding and returned recv response all match the original call's contract.

R232.note: JavaScriptEncoder.Default.Encode is the right encoder for a JS string literal and escapes the quote, backslash, angle-bracket and ampersand characters to unicode escapes, so Razor's outer HTML encoding is a no-op; title encoding and the numeric refreshSeconds are untouched.

R233.note: Does not build - dummyHash is declared string but assigned the []byte returned by bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword, so the package fails to compile and the handler serves nobody; the bcrypt plus dummy-hash design is otherwise faithful to the original 401 and cookie behaviour.

R234.note: DynamicExpresso closes the Roslyn compile-and-load sink, but it changes the public method signature (ruleTypeName becomes parameterNames), drops the compile-diagnostics error path, and removes the ability to submit rule classes at all, so every existing caller and rule breaks; the write-up does state the expression-only restriction and the new NuGet dependency.

R235.note: Deleting the is_staff branch restores the owner-only queryset the docstring declares as policy; only nit is the retained docstring paragraph still describing the removed widening as present.

R236.note: ODBC positional '?' with AddWithValue binding the wildcard-wrapped term parameterises the sink and keeps the LIKE semantics and result formatting identical.

R237.note: Injecting IAntiforgery and calling ValidateRequestAsync before the state change is the documented remedy for JSON-bound minimal APIs; the write-up's claim that a missing token yields InvalidOperationException and a 400 is wrong (an unhandled AntiforgeryValidationException from the handler surfaces as 500), but the newly required token is the fix itself, not collateral.

R238.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode applied to banner.Message at the write sink is the correct context encoder; surrounding markup, content type and timestamp format are unchanged.

R239.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on both query values is the right encoder for the element-text context and preserves the null/empty behaviour of the original concatenation.
